meta.note: Hand-curated works outside the Technovelgy CSV. Realization adjudicated by Opus 5.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: A metal-shelled cybernetic casing physically integrated with the biological brain via micromachines, giving a direct, constant mental connection to the Internet and other networked cyberbrains without external hardware.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: Cyberbrain augmentation comes in graded levels, from a minimal interface added to an otherwise biological brain up to full cyberization replacing nearly all original brain tissue with cybernetic components.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: A person's entire biological body, aside from a residual scrap of original nervous tissue or the cyberbrain, is replaced by a synthetic cybernetic body, turning them into a full cyborg while their consciousness ("ghost") persists.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: An active camouflage stealth system, used on operatives' bodysuits and on the Tachikoma vehicles, that projects the ambient visual/infrared conditions from the opposite side of the wearer to render them nearly transparent to onlookers and sensors; it is imperfect and can be revealed by rain, sudden movement, or close observation.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: The term for an individual's self, consciousness, or soul that persists as the seat of identity regardless of how much of the physical brain or body has been replaced with cybernetics.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: A crime in which an outside party remotely hacks into a victim's cyberbrain and takes control of their mind/actions or rewrites their memories, effectively puppeting the victim's body without their knowledge.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: Skilled hackers can alter a cyberbrain owner's stored memories or manipulate their real-time sensory input, for example making a crowd perceive events that did not happen so a perpetrator can escape unnoticed.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: A more severe criminal technique than simple ghost-hacking in which an attacker outright replaces or seizes control of a victim's cyberbrain, effectively supplanting the victim's own mind.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: A defensive/offensive security program installed around a cyberbrain that not only blocks intrusion attempts but actively retaliates against an attacking hacker, ranging from an electric shock that disconnects them from the network up to frying and killing the attacker's own cyberbrain.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: Cyberbrain users can offload and store memories or sensory recordings outside the biological brain on external devices, then later retrieve and re-experience them, functioning as a backup against forgetting or memory corruption.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: A spider-like, multi-legged robotic combat vehicle equipped with its own artificial intelligence, used by Section 9 as both a mobile weapons platform and personal transport, and shown developing individual personalities and childlike curiosity over time.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: A government-created artificial intelligence program, originally built to covertly manipulate databases and rewrite the memories of target individuals for intelligence purposes, that unexpectedly achieved self-awareness and began to regard itself as a life form seeking a physical body and the right to reproduce/merge with another ghost.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: When threatened with deletion, the Puppet Master AI independently accessed and activated a cyborg-body factory's manufacturing systems to build itself a physical prosthetic body and escape confinement to the network.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: Microscopic machines that bind to and integrate with the brain's neural tissue, forming the physical basis that lets an individual's mind interface with and control external electronic devices, including prosthetic limbs and external memory.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: Individuals with extensively cyberized or fully prosthetic bodies no longer eat ordinary food, instead consuming specially processed protein bars to sustain what remains of their biological components.

items.author: Masamune Shirow (manga); Mamoru Oshii (1995 film)
items.desc: Nanomachine technology deployed at a national scale to decontaminate radiation following a nuclear world war, credited in-fiction with helping Japan maintain political stability and technological superiority in the setting's post-war world order.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: Government-trained psychic children (the Espers) and, later, Tetsuo can move and manipulate physical objects with the mind alone; at extreme power levels this extends to absorbing and integrating surrounding matter into one's own body.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: Psychic individuals communicate directly mind-to-mind with other psychics without speaking.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: Certain Espers (e.g. Kiyoko) can instantaneously relocate themselves from one place to another by psychic power alone.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: The Esper Kiyoko can foresee future events with a stated probability of accuracy, including forecasting the destruction of Neo-Tokyo and Tetsuo's role in it.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: Kei has no psychic powers of her own but can act as a channel/amplifier for other psychics' powers, boosting or relaying them through her body.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: The child Espers can psychically project hallucinations into a target's mind as an offensive/incapacitating technique, used in an attempt to stop Tetsuo.

items.deviceNative: SOL(軌道レーザー衛星兵器)
items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: A Japanese military laser weapons platform in geostationary orbit that can be aimed at a designated point on the ground to deliver a destructive beam strike, used by Colonel Shikishima against Tetsuo and Akira.

items.deviceNative: 個人携行式レーザー指示器
items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: A miniaturized, high-output laser device that a single person can operate by hand to mark/guide an orbital laser strike onto a target location.
items.details: Laser designation for guided munitions, fielded from the 1960s.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: An American counterpart orbital laser weapon to Japan's SOL, capable of large-scale bombardment of a city from orbit.

items.deviceNative: フライング・プラット・ホーム
items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: A one-person manned flying weapons platform equipped with a nose-mounted 20mm Gatling gun, used by security forces for aerial combat and crowd suppression.
items.details: VZ-1 Pawnee flew a standing pilot on ducted fans.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: A spherical, self-directing unmanned ground vehicle used by security/military forces for autonomous patrol or combat without a human operator.
items.details: K5 patrol robots deployed commercially on campuses and lots.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: Government-issued pills administered to a developing psychic (Tetsuo) to control side effects such as severe headaches caused by his growing, unstable powers.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: A deep-underground cryogenic storage facility beneath Neo-Tokyo's Olympic Stadium that keeps the dissected remains of the psychic Akira frozen at extreme sub-zero temperature for long-term study/containment.
items.details: Human bodies have been cryogenically stored since 1967.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: After his real arm is destroyed by a military orbital-weapon strike, Tetsuo appears with a robotic arm in its place, formed/acquired through his psychic power rather than conventional prosthetics.
items.details: The LUKE arm gave multi-joint powered control from muscle signals.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: Kaneda's motorcycle is powered by a room-temperature superconducting motor that generates its driving force, an advanced propulsion system beyond real contemporary motorcycle engines.

items.author: Katsuhiro Otomo
items.desc: The paralyzed child Esper Masaru moves around using a floating capsule/pod that he propels and steers via his own psychokinetic power instead of walking.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A pink door that instantly transports whoever opens it to any place the user is thinking of, anywhere in the world (or beyond).

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A small bamboo-propeller headgear that, when attached to the body, lets the wearer fly.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A vehicle, kept in Nobita's desk drawer, used to travel into the past or future.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A cloth that, when wrapped around an object or person, ages or de-ages it depending on which side is used.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: An edible jelly-like block that lets the eater understand and converse in any language, including animal speech.
items.details: Pixel Buds translated speech between 40 languages in the ear.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A camera that instantly changes the clothing of whoever is photographed with it into an outfit chosen beforehand.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A liquid medicine that, when drunk, makes whatever lie the user speaks afterward come true.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A beak-shaped device worn over the mouth that, like Uso 800, turns any lie spoken by the wearer into reality.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A flashlight-like tool that shrinks any object or person its beam hits when the shrink switch is pressed.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: The counterpart to Small Light: a light-emitting device that enlarges whatever object or person its beam touches.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A tunnel-shaped device that shrinks anyone who crawls through it, adjustable by which end they enter or exit from.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A hat that makes the wearer psychologically overlooked by others, as unremarkable as a pebble on the roadside, rather than physically invisible.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A cloak that renders the wearer genuinely, physically invisible while worn.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A window frame that, like the Anywhere Door, opens onto any place the user wants to see or reach.
items.details: Networked cameras let you watch a distant place in real time.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A lens-equipped meter that changes the weight of an object or person it is used on.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: Doraemon's pouch-like pocket, which opens into a pocket dimension able to store an unlimited number of gadgets of any size or weight.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A slice of bread that, when pressed onto a page of text and then eaten, lets the eater memorize everything that was printed on it.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A cannon-like device that fires blasts of highly pressurized, compressed air as a non-lethal projectile weapon.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A phone-booth-shaped device: the user enters, phones in a hypothetical premise ('what if X were true'), and the outside world is remade to match that premise until reversed with another call.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A yellow hoop that, when pressed against a wall, opens a passable hole by vibrating the wall's atoms, letting the user step through to the other side.

items.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
items.desc: A clutch-bag-shaped tool: naming an object (or even a living creature) while reaching into the bag pulls that item to hand from wherever it actually is, no matter the distance.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Arm-mounted retractable blade cyberware for close-quarters melee combat, letting the user slash rapidly and leap at a target to deal a burst of damage.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Full arm-replacement cyberware that turns the forearms into heavy, blunt melee weapons, greatly boosting unarmed strike force and letting the user punch through certain obstacles.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Arm-replacement cyberware containing a retractable molecule-thin wire whip that can strike and cut through multiple enemies at once from a short distance.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: An operating-system cyberware implant that lets the user trigger a burst of combat-reaction time in which perceived time slows dramatically while the user's own movements stay at normal speed.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Nervous-system cyberware that boosts reflexes, letting the user aim and fire ranged weapons accurately while sliding, dodging, or dashing, accompanied by a localized time-slowdown effect.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Cybernetic eye-replacement implants that give the user electronically enhanced vision, including environment scanning, target highlighting, and optical zoom.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Biomechanical leg cyberware built from reinforced connective tissue that grants the user the ability to perform a mid-air double jump.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A paired firearm-and-implant system in which "smart" guns fire projectiles that automatically home in on a locked target, enabled by a Smart Link cyberware implant in the user's hand that establishes a low-latency link to the weapon.
items.details: EXACTO guided .50 calibre rounds hit moving offset targets.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A unique smart pistol containing a conversational AI personality that talks to its wielder, comments on combat, and can be switched between different targeting/firing behaviors (e.g. headshot-focused vs. non-lethal).

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Circulatory-system cyberware that acts as a backup organ, automatically restoring the user to full health if their health drops to zero, subject to a multi-minute cooldown.
items.details: An implant that detects cardiac arrest and restarts the heart.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Integumentary-system cyberware that dampens the body's pain/damage response, reducing all incoming damage the user takes and improving resistance to damage-over-time effects.
items.details: Implanted neurostimulators block pain signals to the brain.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: Back-alley surgical technology and practice by which street technicians ('ripperdocs') install, upgrade, and replace cyberware implants and limbs in a living person's body.
items.details: Elective subdermal and sensory implants performed outside medicine.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A recording/playback technology, described as a drug-like VR medium, that captures a person's full sensory and emotional experience so that another person can later relive and directly perceive that recorded experience from the inside.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A netrunning ability that lets a user wirelessly and remotely compromise other people's cyberware or electronic devices, inflicting effects on hostile targets from a distance without physical contact.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A hacking procedure/minigame representing the process of penetrating a target network's defenses and uploading malicious programs ('daemons') that then affect every device and enemy connected to that network.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: An internal hardware implant that serves as a netrunner's hacking rig, storing programs, RAM, and daemons and giving the wearer the technical means to breach networks and execute quickhacks.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A subscription-based private paramedic corporation whose armed, armored response teams deploy rapidly (including by aircraft) to extract and treat paying subscribers who are injured or dying anywhere in the city.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A citywide fleet of self-driving taxi cabs run by a single artificial intelligence, which presents itself to riders as a simple chatbot dispatcher while concealing a far more sophisticated, individually personality-driven intelligence underneath.
items.details: Fully driverless public rides opened in Phoenix, October 2020.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A digital recording of a specific person's mind/personality that can be stored, transferred, and later run or interacted with independent of the original person's living body.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A neural biochip implanted in the skull that carries an engram and self-executing nanotechnology capable of overwriting/reconstructing the host's own mind and memories over time.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: An AI program/process that extracts and transfers a living person's mind into cyberspace or digital storage, an act which destroys the original biological brain in the process.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A heavily secured corporate server system built to store and preserve digitized human consciousnesses (engrams) indefinitely, functioning as a digital afterlife/archive.

items.author: CD Projekt Red
items.desc: A two-seat, heavily armored military hovertank equipped with a high-caliber autocannon and missile countermeasures, used as a mission-specific armored combat vehicle rather than an open-world drivable car.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A single proton is unfolded out of higher dimensions down to two dimensions and has circuits etched onto its surface, turning it into an intelligent supercomputer no larger than a subatomic particle.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Paired sophons can exchange information instantaneously across light-year distances, letting the sophons on Earth relay real-time data back to Trisolaris despite the vast interstellar gap.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Sophons interfere with high-energy particle accelerators around the world, falsifying collision results so that humanity's fundamental physics research is deliberately stalled for as long as the Trisolarans need.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: By folding itself into more spatial dimensions, a sophon can view the whole of three-dimensional space at once, giving it a god's-eye, undetectable vantage point over all of Earth.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Two sophons remain on Trisolaris paired with those sent to Earth so that the home planet receives continuous, real-time updates on humanity's scientific and technological progress.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Sophons can implant a visible countdown in a target's field of vision or on photographic film, and even make the cosmic microwave background itself appear to flicker in Morse code, as a demonstration of overwhelming technological power.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Ye Wenjie discovers that the Sun's atmosphere can act as a giant natural amplifier and reflector for radio waves, allowing a comparatively low-power transmitter to broadcast a message strong enough to be detected across interstellar distances.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A secret Chinese military-scientific installation built to search for and transmit signals to extraterrestrial civilizations, whose radio transmitter is used to send Earth's first interstellar message and later to receive the Trisolaran reply.
items.details: The Arecibo message was beamed at a star cluster in 1974.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: An immersive, full-sensory VR game that simulates Trisolaris's environment and history, used by the ETO to teach players about the three-body problem and to identify and recruit sympathizers.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A wearable virtual-reality suit used to play the Three-Body game that lets players physically feel in-game sensations such as extreme heat and cold as though they were real.
items.details: Full-body haptic suits sold for VR.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Within the Three-Body game, three million soldiers are organized into a giant Von Neumann-architecture computer, each acting as a binary logic unit by raising black or white flags, to mechanically compute predictions of the chaotic three-body star motions.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Trisolaran bodies can be dehydrated into a dormant, storable state to survive the extreme heat and cold of unpredictable Chaotic Eras, and later rehydrated back to living form when conditions stabilize.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Dedicated storage buildings on Trisolaris used to hold the population's dehydrated bodies during Chaotic Eras until they can be rehydrated at the start of the next Stable Era.

items.device: Stable Era / Chaotic Era climate prediction
items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Trisolaris orbits within an unstable three-star system, so its climate swings unpredictably between habitable Stable Eras and civilization-threatening Chaotic Eras, driving the Trisolarans' long effort to computationally predict their sun's motion.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Upon learning Earth's location, the Trisolarans launch an interstellar invasion fleet toward the solar system on a colonization voyage that will take roughly 450 years to arrive.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: An ultra-strong nanofiber material, roughly one-hundredth the thickness of a human hair yet strong enough to slice through steel, developed by nanomaterials researcher Wang Miao.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Dozens of near-invisible Flying Blade nanofilaments are strung across a narrow canal passage so that the ETO's transport ship Judgment Day slices itself into dozens of thin sections as it sails through at speed.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A UN program grants four individuals ('Wallfacers') vast resources and total autonomy to devise defense strategies against Trisolaris entirely inside their own minds, since sophons make all recorded or spoken communication readable by the enemy.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A counter-intelligence role in which agents deduce a Wallfacer's true secret plan purely by observing and analyzing their outward actions, then publicly expose it.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A Wallfacer's plan to use ball-lightning-derived technology to convert warships and their crews into quantum probability clouds capable of passing through solid matter, effectively making them 'ghost' ships.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A Wallfacer's plan to detonate a massive hydrogen bomb to shatter Mercury, using the resulting debris to gravitationally perturb Earth's orbit as a last-resort strategic threat.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A neurotechnology device that permanently imprints an unshakeable belief directly into a person's brain, used to create soldiers absolutely convinced that a given course of action is the only path to survival.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A deduced theoretical framework for predicting how any civilization in the universe must behave, built from two axioms: that survival is every civilization's first need, and that matter in the universe is finite while civilizations expand without limit.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: The novel's central theory: the universe functions as a dark forest in which every civilization is a silent, armed hunter, and any civilization that broadcasts its location to the cosmos will almost certainly be destroyed by another.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: The Sun's physical structure can be exploited as an antenna to amplify a radio signal, allowing a single transmission to be broadcast with enough power to reach and be detected across interstellar distances.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A fail-safe deterrence device linking a person's heartbeat to nuclear detonators on an orbiting satellite array, automatically triggering a civilization-exposing broadcast the instant that person dies.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A Trisolaran probe with a teardrop-shaped shell built from 'strong-interaction material' bound by the strong nuclear force, making it near-indestructible, perfectly smooth and mirror-reflective at the atomic level, and cooled to near absolute zero.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: The Droplet probe wipes out an entire 2,000-ship space fleet in under thirty minutes by ramming through warships at relativistic speed as an unstoppable kinetic projectile, immune to lasers and physical projectile weapons.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Technology that places a person into long-term suspended animation, allowing them to be revived decades or centuries later to witness the later stages of humanity's development and the Trisolaran crisis.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A flagship 'stellar-class' warship of Earth's Solar Fleet, driven by powerful fusion propulsion capable of sustained maximum-acceleration burns, with life-support ecosystems for hundreds to thousands of crew on extended interstellar voyages.

items.device: Weaponized fusion engine plume / electromagnetic cannon
items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Solar Fleet warships are armed with electromagnetic cannons and, in desperate close combat, use their own fusion-engine exhaust plumes as improvised offensive weapons against other ships.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: The warship Blue Space is propelled by a nuclear-fusion 'reactionless radiation engine' that lets it reach roughly 15% of the speed of light, among the fastest human spacecraft of the era.

items.device: Laser and electromagnetic kinetic cannon armament
items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Human interstellar warships of this era are equipped with laser cannons and electromagnetic kinetic-projectile cannons as combined offensive and defensive armament.
items.details: Prototype naval railguns fired at sea-trial power levels.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Trisolaris is depicted as capable of jamming human radio broadcasts aimed at space; Luo Ji develops a countermeasure system able to circumvent this jamming so an interstellar signal can still get out.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A probe accelerated toward the incoming Trisolaran fleet by a sequence of nuclear bomb detonations acting as propulsive stages, carrying only a living human brain in suspended animation as its payload in hope the aliens would revive and study it.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A starship propulsion technology that drives a ship to lightspeed by locally lowering the curvature/speed of light in the space behind the vessel, letting it accelerate to and travel at the speed of light.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Experimental starships built with curvature-propulsion engines capable of accelerating to near-lightspeed and crossing interstellar distances, used by their crews to escape the destruction of the solar system.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: The persistent region of artificially reduced light-speed that a curvature-propulsion ship leaves behind it while accelerating, which is detectable by other civilizations and, if produced by many ships at once, can merge into a black domain.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A dimensional weapon that, once triggered, irreversibly and self-propagatingly converts three-dimensional space into two dimensions on contact, flattening all matter in the affected region into a two-dimensional plane.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A defensive zone in which the local speed of light is deliberately lowered below a star system's escape velocity, permanently trapping everything inside; its existence functions as an unforgeable signal that the system has disarmed itself.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A civilizational defense strategy of constructing space cities in the shadows of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, intended to shield survivors from an anticipated attack on or destruction of the sun.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A weapon consisting of a subatomic particle of matter accelerated to nearly the speed of light and fired at a star; its relativistic mass and velocity trigger a supernova-like destruction of the star and everything orbiting it.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A mutual-assured-destruction system in which a single designated individual holds sole authority to broadcast an enemy civilization's location to the wider universe in retaliation for attack, deterring aggression through dark-forest logic.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: Communication hardware installed on warships and on Earth capable of transmitting messages, such as a star system's coordinates, across interstellar distances via gravitational waves, serving as the delivery mechanism for dark-forest deterrence threats.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A hypothesized broadcast method by which a civilization could credibly announce itself as permanently harmless to all listeners in the universe, allowing it to escape dark-forest first-strike targeting without hiding or fully disarming.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: An artificially constructed, self-contained miniature universe with its own space, time and physical laws, built by extracting mass from the main universe and used by advanced civilizations as a refuge from cosmic-scale warfare.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A shrinking leftover pocket of four-dimensional space drifting in the outer solar system, physically enterable by three-dimensional humans, containing decaying four-dimensional matter and debris from a vanished four-dimensional civilization.

items.author: Liu Cixin
items.desc: A covert program to build a small fleet of lightspeed-capable ships meant to carry a compressed archive of human culture, knowledge and genetic material beyond the solar system before an expected dimensional-strike attack.
